reason: The recorded image ID has never been reproduced from these inputs, and this stamp does not
endorse it. It is very probably stale: ImageID.sol last changed on 2026-06-23 in 8b81f51c,
while the guest and the journal types changed on 2026-08-06 in f716d933b and again on
2026-08-13 in 02ebe4589. The second of those replaced a four-field result with a nine-field
domain-separated journal.
The digest is a drift baseline, rebaselined whenever a guest input changes for a reason that
is understood. It has moved three times. First when this stamp was introduced. Second when
crates/support/methods/guest/Cargo.lock was repaired: it was one line behind its manifests, so
'cargo metadata --locked' refused the workspace and the reproducible build stopped before it
started. Third for the two changes below.
0. The support workspace was repaired to build against the moved pin at all. The new revision
carries the InputPolicy API, and crates/support still called the previous signatures, so
`cargo check --locked` failed outright. The guest now passes the user program's `policy()`
rather than assuming the default, and the program exposes one. Those files are guest inputs,
so the digest moved with them.
1. The guest pin moved from c2097da6 to 5b2ca661. The old pin predated every fix to the code
the guest compiles, among them 5213e23d, which derives the guest input root from the
processed ciphertexts. The rationale in crates/support/Cargo.toml has the details.
2. crates/support/methods/build.rs now takes the guest builder image tag from ARG
RISC0_TOOLCHAIN in crates/support/Dockerfile. risc0-build does not read that Dockerfile; it
generates its own and, left alone, used its compiled-in default of r0.1.88.0, carrying rustc
1.88. The guest's dependency tree pins fhe.rs at an MSRV of 1.91.1, so the guest could not
compile at all, while check-image-id.sh compared the Dockerfile against rust-toolchain.toml
and found them in agreement. That check was asserting a toolchain the ELF build never got.
The rebuild still does not complete, and the remaining failure is not understood. With the
toolchain corrected the build reaches fhe 0.2.1, whose build script reports 'protoc failed:'
with no diagnostic. No protoc exists anywhere in the builder image and PROTOC is unset, so
fhe's own is_protoc_available guard should have skipped proto compilation entirely. It did not.
The attempts so far ran the linux/amd64 builder image emulated on arm64, which is the first
thing to rule out: run .github/workflows/rebuild-guest-image-id.yml, which does the same
rebuild on a native amd64 runner and uploads the regenerated ImageID.sol and this stamp.
Until that succeeds, nothing ties the image ID the deployed verifier enforces to the guest
source in this tree. Note also that CRISP does not deploy this image ID: it deploys the one in
examples/CRISP/.interfold/generated/contracts/ImageID.sol, built from its own e3-user-program,
which this script does not check and which is older still.
